The single stress remark (footnote 13, p. 1232) is about Gele' (Kele), not Ponam: 'Stress, although phonemic, tends to fall on long vowels, on the penultimate of reduplicated forms, on the final syllable of noun stem followed by possessive enclitics, and in other instances on the final syllable of words.'

sources.note: 'A Note on Usage' (pp. xiii-xiv): Ponam spelling 'basically follows Pidgin pronunciation' except j = English y and an unwritten w after m and p; no plural marking. Nothing on stress. Ch. 1 cites Healey 1976 and Schooling & Schooling on Ponam's closeness to Andra and Sori.

sources.note: Nothing for Ponam: Ponam appears only in the genetic tree, consonant-correspondence Table 36 (p-; p/_u; f) and cognate sets; the only 'stress' passages in the book concern Ali (ch. 3) and *ai reduction. No suprasegmental statement for any Admiralty language.
